document.abstract: Advanced, low-latency MPEG-4 AVC HD codecs, coupled with the appropriate DVB-T modulation and FEC parameters, allow news teams to use the production techniques traditionally used in SD-ENG, such as field-to-studio interviews and multiple camera feeds, in HD-ENG, without jeopardizing the quality of the production or the integrity of the HD signal. The goal is to provide an ENG news team with the tools that allow them to cover live news events in HD and with high confidence in “getting the shot” back to the studio.

authors.bio: John L. Pittas is currently with Evertz Microsystems, Ltd., in Burlington, Ontario. Before joining Evertz, Pittas provided technology, marketing, sales and business development guidance for Fujitsu's MPEG-4 AVC codec products to Fujitsu Computer Products of America, Inc.‘s (FCPA's) New Products Group, and strategic technology and business development planning for television broadcast products to Fujitsu's Strategic Planning Office. He was instrumental in introducing Fujitsu's MPEG-4 AVC HD codecs into the U.S. broadcast market. Pittas has over 30 years of experience in film and video production, video circuit and system design, and broadcast product and engineering management. Before joining FCPA, Pittas served as vice president of broadcast products and engineering at SeaChange, where he led the development and launch of the company's broadcast product line with the Broadcast MediaCluster, the Broadcast MediaLibrary, and the MediaClient codecs. The Broadcast MediaCluster was awarded an Emmy by the National Academy of Television Arts and Sciences in 2001. Pittas currently holds four patents in video data manipulation and transmission technology and is a member of SMPTE and the Institute for Electrical and Electronics Engineers.
